## The original papers

> Alexandre Quemy, Marc Schoenauer. *True Pareto Fronts for Multi-Objective AI Planning
> Instances.* European Conference on Combinatorial Optimization, EvoCOP 2015, Copenhagen,
> LNCS 9026, Springer, pp. 197–208, 2015. [hal-01109777](https://hal.science/hal-01109777).

> Alexandre Quemy, Marc Schoenauer, Johann Dréo.
> [arXiv:2304.14659](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.14659), 2023. Extends the approach to
> non-symmetric durations.

> Alexandre Quemy, Marc Schoenauer, Vincent Vidal, Johann Dréo, Pierre Savéant. *Solving Large
> MultiZenoTravel Benchmarks with Divide-and-Evolve.* Learning and Intelligent Optimization,
> LION 9, Lille, LNCS 8994, Springer, pp. 262–267, 2015.
> [hal-01109776](https://hal.science/hal-01109776).

The model, the benchmark and the first ZenoSolver (2016) are those of these papers. Please cite
them for MultiZenoTravel.

## This project

The current solver `zeno`, the theory note `doc/theory/exact-front.md`, the Lean 4 formalization in
`lean/`, the certificate format and checkers, the benchmarks and this website are the work of
**Alexandre Quemy**, in the repository
[`aquemy/ZenoSolver`](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver).

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Attribution and fair use.** Throughout the [blueprint](proofs.qmd), the papers' statements and
proofs are reproduced **verbatim** in grey boxes marked *From the original paper*, with the paper,
section and page, solely for scholarly comparison with the note and the formalization. That
material remains its authors' and publishers'. The blue and green boxes hold this project's
contribution.
:::

## What the note corrects

The note's §5 and §6 and the draft erratum
([`doc/erratum.md`](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/doc/erratum.md)) give the
details. In short:

### The per-PPP greedy is not optimal {#f1}

Both papers fix a multiset of landings (a PPP) and schedule it greedily, longest flights first onto
the least-loaded plane (EvoCOP 2015 Algorithm 1, arXiv §3.2), and claim the result is the optimal
makespan of that PPP. It is not. On $d = (6, 10)$, $c = (40, 20)$, $t = 5$, $p = 2$ the 2016 solver
misses the front point (260, 60) ([§5](proofs.qmd#node-s5)). That front is checked by the Lean
kernel alone (`Examples.lptCounterexample_front`). No polynomial per-PPP rule can be exact unless
P = NP: deciding whether a multiset of landings can be flown within a makespan is strongly
NP-complete ([Theorem 8.1](proofs.qmd#node-theorem-8-1)).

### Proposition I holds only for the front {#f2}

"Pareto-optimal plans use exactly $2t - p$ central cities" is false for plans: with zero costs, a
plan with more landings can be Pareto-optimal. What holds is the front statement: the front is
the Pareto set of $(c(X), M(X))$ over multisets $X$ of $2t - p$ landings, with $M(X)$ the least
makespan of an **admissible** partition of $X$
([Corollary 4.8](proofs.qmd#node-corollary-4-8), machine-checked).

### Waiting can be harmful in the non-symmetric case {#f3}

The arXiv paper's non-symmetric argument assumes that no plane has to wait harmfully for a
passenger. That is false, even with no central flights and under the triangle inequality
([Conjecture 6.5, refuted](proofs.qmd#node-conjecture-6-5);
[Proposition 6.5](proofs.qmd#node-proposition-6-5)). The note replaces the assumption with
*schedulable domination* ([Theorem 6.9](proofs.qmd#node-theorem-6-9), machine-checked for every
plan). An exhaustive search over role configurations with exact schedules is therefore sound, and
`zeno` uses it to close such gaps.

### The pairing argument without (A1) is incomplete {#f4}

Without (A1), the arXiv pairing argument concludes "lower cost" from a set inclusion and
"dominates" from per-pattern durations; both steps fail
([Conjecture 4.10](proofs.qmd#node-conjecture-4-10), open). Without (A1) the front is still
certified wherever the relaxation $L$ meets the achieved cost, which covers every front of the
default generator ([Theorem 10.1](proofs.qmd#node-theorem-10-1)).

### What still holds {#holds}

The model, the flight patterns, the lower bound of $2t - p$ landings, and the no-waiting
construction of a plan from an admissible partition
([Theorem 4.1](proofs.qmd#node-theorem-4-1), machine-checked). On the default generator the
front is known in closed form, and the published benchmark fronts of that family are probably
right despite the greedy (Conjecture 10.2, checked on 115 instances, not proved).

## Honesty: what is proved, and how {#honesty}

{{< include _blueprint-stats.md >}}

The blueprint's badges are computed when the site is built, from `collectAxioms` on the Lean
declarations each node lists. A node is badged machine-checked only if the declarations that
formalise its **whole** statement are axiom-clean theorems. Declarations covering only part of a
statement are listed under it, with their own badges, and the node keeps the note's status. The
generator stops if a declaration is missing or a label is not found in the note.

The compiled tools add trust in the Lean compiler and in an unverified parser
([trust base](solver/lean.qmd#trust)).

## This website

Built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) from `site/` into `docs/`
([how](solver/install.qmd#this-website)). The blueprint pages are generated from
`site/blueprint.toml`, the theory note and the Lean sources by `site/gen_blueprint.py`; the tables
from the committed baselines by `site/gen_pages.py`; the claim graph and the history from the
knowledge commits and `claims.toml` by `site/gen_graph.py`. The paper excerpts are in
`site/paper/`.
